okta_admin_roles._comment: Lab 37 (Okta Professional 1.3/1.2). Role capabilities follow the Okta Help Center pages 'Standard administrator roles and permissions', 'Help desk administrators' and 'Role permissions' (custom admin roles), Identity Engine, read 2026-11-05. The 'okta.*' permission names follow Okta's custom-role permission naming; the 'std.*' names are this course's own labels for abilities that only standard roles have (there is no custom-role permission for them). Simplified: real roles carry many more abilities than modelled here. Re-check against the Help Center before relying on a detail.

okta.users.lifecycle.manage.description: activate, deactivate, suspend and delete users

okta.users.lifecycle.clearSessions.description: clear users' Okta sessions and tokens

okta.apps.manage.description: add, configure and delete app integrations

okta.apps.assignment.manage.description: assign users and groups to apps

std.admins.manage.description: add and remove administrators and assign admin roles

Organization Administrator._comment: Org admins do not manage apps (Help Center comparison table). They can clear sessions of super admins but cannot reset their passwords.

Group Administrator._comment: Group admins cannot create groups or manage group rules. 'manages_other_admins: false' is this course's conservative reading; the Help Center table only spells out super-admin targets.

Help Desk Administrator._comment: Fixed set: reset password, reset MFA, unlock, clear sessions, view users in assigned groups. Cannot create, suspend or delete users or assign apps or groups. May clear super admins' sessions but not reset their passwords.

manage_group_membership.description: add and remove members of groups

manage_admins.description: assign admin roles to people and groups

plan_definitions.STANDARD_ROLE: assign the least-privileged standard admin role, constrained where the role allows it
plan_definitions.CUSTOM_ROLE: build a custom admin role with only the listed permissions and bind it to a resource set
plan_definitions.ESCALATE: make no assignment; send the request to the identity team

denial_definitions.UNKNOWN_ACTION: the action is not in the permission catalogue
denial_definitions.NOT_ASSIGNED: the actor holds no admin role, directly or through a group
denial_definitions.MISSING_PERMISSION: none of the actor's roles includes the permission
denial_definitions.OUTSIDE_SCOPE: the target is outside the role's constraint or resource set
denial_definitions.PROTECTED_ADMIN_TARGET: the target is an administrator, or an admin group, that the role may not change

finding_definitions.SUPER_ADMIN_EXCESS: more people hold Super Administrator than policy allows
finding_definitions.CUSTOM_ROLE_EMPTY_RESOURCE_SET: a custom role is bound to a missing or empty resource set, so it governs nothing
finding_definitions.UNSCOPED_ROLE: a role that could be constrained applies to the whole org with no recorded reason
finding_definitions.ROLE_ASSIGNED_TO_INDIVIDUAL: an admin role is assigned to one person instead of to a group

concepts.standard admin role: One of Okta's built-in administrator roles, such as Help Desk Administrator, with a fixed set of permissions.
concepts.custom admin role: A role you build by picking individual permissions, used when no standard role is narrow enough.
concepts.resource set: The collection of users, groups or apps that a custom role assignment is allowed to act on.
concepts.role constraint: A limit placed on a standard role so it applies only to chosen groups or apps instead of the whole org.
concepts.admin group: A group that has an admin role assigned; only super admins can change its membership.
concepts.group rule: An Okta rule that adds users to a group automatically when their profile attributes match an expression.
concepts.least privilege: Give each administrator only the permissions and the targets their job needs, and nothing more.
